title: The Vow of Maple Hollow
premise: Kestrel Ashgrove has spent ten years building Maple Hollow Café into her safe harbor after a scandal destroyed her first career, sustained only by anonymous letters from a pen pal she's never met. When the letters' author — Elias Vane, heir to the corrupt vineyard dynasty that ruined her — moves in next door, Kestrel discovers he wrote to atone for his family's sins without ever confessing who he was. As the vineyard's first harvest approaches and his father moves to seize her café block for expansion, Kestrel must choose between a career-saving contract that requires her silence and exposing the truth that would save Maple Hollow but break them both. She chooses the town, testifies against the Vanes, and finds that Elias, stripped of his name and fortune, chooses her freely — they open the harvest festival together, no longer strangers.
about_author: Petra Underhill is the pen name of a former small-town baker who traded early mornings at the oven for early mornings at the keyboard. She writes romances about second chances, stubborn communities, and the people brave enough to be truly seen.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A bank notice arrives at Maple Hollow Café on the morning of the autumn fair; Kestrel masks panic behind perfect laminated dough while her found family of regulars unknowingly steadies her. Beat: fear hidden under competence.

chapters.title: The Letter That Never Came
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Flashback woven through present: ten years of letters from 'E,' the stranger who talked her through rebuilding her life. This month's letter is late, and its absence feels like losing a limb. Beat: longing and quiet dread.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A moving truck blocks her alley; the man unloading boxes is distractingly kind and oddly familiar with her habits. He introduces himself as Eli Vance, renting the cottage next door. Beat: wary curiosity, first spark.

chapters.title: Flour and Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Eli, revealed to readers as Elias Vane, watches Kestrel through her window and nearly confesses everything over borrowed sugar. His father's voicemail about the vineyard acquisition interrupts. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Harvest Contract
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Vane Vineyard offers Maple Hollow a lucrative dessert partnership — enough to erase her debt — if she signs an exclusivity clause. Her best friend Dana urges caution; pride says sign. Beat: hope tangled in a trap.

chapters.title: Letters, Old and New
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Rereading his own sent letters, Eli realizes Kestrel knows his handwriting from the vineyard's public correspondence. He begins writing to her again by hand, leaving notes unsigned at her door. Beat: cowardice disguised as romance.

chapters.title: Cinnamon at Midnight
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Insomnia baking turns into a shared 2 a.m. kitchen session when Eli appears at her back door. They trade half-truths; the chemistry is undeniable and terrifying. First kiss, interrupted by her phone: another overdue notice. Beat: intimacy shadowed by secrecy.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana recalls the scandal that ended Kestrel's first career — a rigged review campaign traced to Vane money — and grows suspicious of the new neighbor's timing. Beat: protective anger, rising stakes.

chapters.title: The Father's Shadow
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. summoned home, Eli endures Aldous Vane's contempt and learns the acquisition targets not just the café but the whole block, displacing the families who took Kestrel in. Beat: the corruption theme made personal.

chapters.title: A Recipe for Two
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel and Eli develop a signature pastry together for the harvest festival — the closest thing to honesty they've had. She almost tells him about 'E'; he almost tells her his name. Beat: tenderness at its peak before the fall.

chapters.title: Handwriting on the Wall
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Signing the contract, Kestrel recognizes the loop of the 'g' in Aldous Vane's signature — identical to her decade of letters from E. She confronts Eli, who admits only to being a Vane, not to the letters. Beat: betrayal, heartbreak, door slammed.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Cast out by Kestrel and pressured by his father, Eli burns his unsent final letter and prepares to leave town. A visit from the widow Marta, whose house is on the block, shames him into staying. Beat: rock bottom, seed of courage.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Grieving, Kestrel throws herself into the contract work and realizes each 'safe step' of her rebuilt life was actually guided by someone who knew her completely. She rereads every letter. Beat: grief turning to clarity.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana and Kestrel dig into vineyard records and find falsified reviews, bribed inspectors, and the paper trail of Kestrel's original ruin. Beat: the power-and-corruption theme surfaces fully; allies assemble.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli offers his father a deal: his silence and inheritance in exchange for dropping the block acquisition. Aldous counters by threatening to expose Eli's letters as manipulation of a vulnerable woman. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: What the Vine Knows
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. On the eve of harvest, Kestrel walks the vineyard rows where it all began and finds Eli's discarded letter — the confession he never sent, naming himself as E. Beat: devastating tenderness; the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the county hearing on the acquisition, Kestrel takes the floor, tears up the contract publicly, and presents the ledgers. Eli stands and corroborates everything against his own family. Beat: climax — both sacrifice their safe things at once.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Aldous retaliates: disinheritance, lawsuits, a press smear. Eli, broke and named, waits outside the darkened café, unable to knock. Beat: consequences landing; love unproven.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel lets him in — not to forgive, but to ask the question she should have asked ten years ago: why the letters? His answer, clumsy and true, is the first thing between them with nothing hidden. Beat: reconciliation earned, not given.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The block's families harvest the vineyard's边缘 rows themselves, claiming the land's fruit as theirs; the café serves the festival crowd debt-free on pre-orders alone. Beat: found family triumphant, community as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Vow
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Under festival lanterns, Eli gives her the one letter he kept — the first — and asks for nothing but a fresh page. She writes back, in front of everyone: stay. Beat: the vow made mutual and public.

chapters.title: Maple Hollow Rising
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Spring: the café expands into the old winery office, co-signed by two names. A letter arrives from a stranger in trouble, and Kestrel answers it — passing on what was given to her. Beat: memory honored, corruption answered with care, future open.
